Previous State Legislation

 ● HB 04-1433: Diagnostic Academic Growth
 Calculation
 • Not to be used for accountability
 • Measures longitudinal growth of students using all available
 years of data
 • Diagnostic information for student sent to district
 • Is student on track to reach proficiency within 3 years or
 by 10th grade.
 • Data was not widely used or discussed
 • Useful process for R&D

2 Education

Current State Legislation

 ● HB 07-1048: Adequate Academic Growth
 • The cornerstone of the state’s accountability
 system
 • Technical Advisory Panel
 • Recommend model to State Board of Education
 • Use model for:
 • Governor’s Improvement Award
 • Determining if students are on track to proficiency within
 3 years or 10th grade

Aggregating Student Growth
 Percentiles

 ● Find the median student growth percentile
 • School
 • Disaggregated group
 • District
 ● Used as the one summary number for growth
 ● Categorized as:
 • Low (less than 35th percentile)
 • Typical (35th- 65th percentiles)
 • High (greater than 65th percentile)

What can we dig for?

 ● Now that we have a more detailed map, we
 need to be clear about what we can find.

 this data can answer, and what it can’t answer

 Colorado Department of
16 Education

STUDENTS AND PARENTS

 ● What the growth model can answer:

 • How much growth did I show relative to other
 students starting at the same place?

 • How much support do I need to get to the next
 proficiency level?

 Colorado Department of
17 Education

STUDENTS AND PARENTS

 ● What the growth measure, along with other
 information* can answer:
 • Is my school able to help students, especially
 students like me, grow as much as I need to?

 • What kinds of support do I need to get to reach my
 goals for proficiency?
 * Other information consists of formative assessment results, knowledge of student and teacher
 needs, analysis of student work, etc.

 Colorado Department of
18 Education

SCHOOL LEVEL

 ● What the growth model can answer:
 • What is the median student growth percentile in our school?
 • How does it compare to other similar schools?
 • How does the median student growth percentile differ
 between different groups of students?
 • How much extra support do our students need to reach
 proficiency?
 • Do we see exceptionally high or low growth anywhere in our
 school?

 Colorado Department of
19 Education

SCHOOL LEVEL

 ● What the growth measure, along with other
 information* can answer:
 • Are certain intervention programs used in our school correlated
 with greater student growth percentiles?
 • Are these interventions leading students to reach proficiency?
 • What may be causing exceptionally high or low growth in our
 school?
 • How can we share what is working well for us?
 • What are realistic school improvement goals for student growth?
 • * Other information consists of formative assessment results, knowledge of student and
 teacher needs, analysis of student work, etc.

 Colorado Department of
20 Education

DISTRICT LEVEL
 ● What the growth model can answer:
 • What is the median student growth percentile in our district?
 • How does it compare with other similar districts?
 • How does the median student growth percentile differ between
 different groups of students?
 • What percent of students are making growth adequate to reach
 proficiency within 3 years?
 • How much extra support do our students need to reach
 proficiency?
 • Do we see exceptionally high or low growth anywhere in our
 district?
 • How are the different schools in our district doing? Are there any
 patterns?

STATE- CDE

PUBLIC

 ● What the growth model can answer:
 • Which schools and districts in Colorado have the highest median
 student growth percentiles?

PUBLIC
